claim: Standalone preprocessing requires closed edits, guards the source, clones construction and returns the transformed graph.
Tests verify culling without an execution plan, source immutability, failure rollback, retained compiled lifetime and execution rejection without a device.
Rules receive a borrowed view; preprocessing can edit or remove graph nodes while compilation receives a const view.
Post-rule validation checks valid definitions, lowered subgraphs/stages, unique names, resources, cycles and required resource ordering.
Exact ordered default preprocessing and compilation rule lists.
Unique producers permit consumer-first authoring; repeated writers use attachment order, select the preceding value and protect readers from overwrites.
Repeated-write, independent-reader and ReadWrite tests establish producer selection and ordering without reader-reader dependencies.
Buffer intervals and texture mip/slice/plane ranges are swept for overlap; reads require complete producer, external or initialization-prefix coverage.
Access validation rejects invalid identities, directions, unknown states, invalid ranges, incompatible buffer states and missing attachment accesses.
Automatic usage is resolved to required capabilities; explicit and imported resources must satisfy requirements and final descriptors are concrete.
Side effects and writes to output, persistent or external resources root a backward traversal through every incoming edge; culling marks nodes rather than deleting them.
Compilation requires a closed preprocessed graph, validates bindings and rules, clones input, prepares nodes, runs ordered rules, validates the result and retains the snapshot.
Preparation preserves transformed semantic descriptions, rehydrates native declarations by provenance, validates requirements and clones stage parameters per assembled draw.
Node requirements combine portable features, CUDA conditions and named read-only environment predicates; declaration validation differs from device admission.
Admission retains compiler-source and subgraph contracts, rechecks explicit requirements, and distinguishes device-independent analysis from inferred native support.
Pipeline inference validates ancestry, respects same-family consumer boundaries, disambiguates groups, combines settings/layouts/stages, validates patterns and computes semantic identity.
The default inference rule validates each live node using its already assembled node-local contributions and shader contracts.
Pipeline contributions, requests, configurations, projected nodes, semantic patterns and resolved native references carry distinct information.
Shader contract validation checks reflected shader schemas, binding layouts and declared resource access coverage.
Rule instances may repeat and execute in list order; invalid custom orders, missing output and exceptions fail without publishing partial results.
The compile result retains input and node state plus execution order, memory proof, queue/stream batches, logical fence edges and diagnostics.
Flattening partitions executable nodes into dispatches; fence resolution preserves topology and alias dependencies through declarations and adds queue/stream chaining.
Final validation checks node partitions, dependencies, allocation/order consistency, batching compatibility, dispatch completeness and required cross-domain fences.
Access declarations identify a resource, read/write direction, required RHI state and buffer or texture subresource range.
Frozen node payloads retain semantic declarations, attachment order and lowering/culling annotations; edge payloads distinguish value and overwrite dependencies.
Rule instances retain immutable configuration, expose stable names and disable adaptive scheduling unless explicitly opted in.
Ordered shared immutable rule instances form the compiler program; rule identity and order participate in revision caching.
Preprocessing rules receive a mutable private graph view.
Compilation rules read a const graph view and refine the unpublished execution result.
